beats.title: B1 HOOK: rule 3 + confession + who ordered it
B2 SETUP + AUTHORITY
B3 INTRUSION: a minor rule broken before it is read (HEARSE-P1 0:31)
B4 FIRST PROOF: the rules are real
B7 LULL + PLANTS (keys, tape)
B8 MIDPOINT: the owner orders the break (rival authorities)
B9 PEAK: the camera monitor (the scariest image, held ~4 s with one change)
B10 LIFELINE + B6 ISOLATION
B12 CLIFF: sound before visual, new imperative, bookend

items.text: Rule three of my night desk. If nineteen-oh-three calls, send nobody up. Nineteen-oh-three is empty.
items.screen: FRAME 0 = COVER: desk-phone close-up, the 1903 button under yellow tape glowing bright red through it; the propped work phone shows the Desk Handover chat with the rule-3 bubble enlarged ("1903" in an alert bubble)

items.text: Tonight I broke rule three. A text from the owner ordered me to.
items.screen: Lock-screen banner flash: "Mr. Pell (Owner) · Go up now." (snap zoom, glitch)

items.text: The concierge before me, Gus, had that desk for thirty-one years. Last night was his last shift.
items.screen: Lobby wide: glass doors, marble desk, elevator behind; Lena small at the desk. Chat header "Desk Handover · 2 members", system line "Gus Brandt · Night Desk · 31 yrs"

items.text: We never met, but he added me to a chat called Desk Handover, with six rules.
items.screen: Banner "Gus added you to Desk Handover"; Gus: "6 rules. Read them twice." then the six rule bubbles stack in fast

items.text: I only read rule three. So at one, when the lobby got stuffy, I propped the glass door open.
items.screen: Desk clock 1:04; the glass door swings open onto the dark street, wastebasket as a wedge

items.text: Behind me, the elevator started coming down by itself, from nineteen.
items.screen: Elevator floor display counting down 19 > 18 > 17 (nobody pressed it)

items.text: Gus texted: Shut the door. Rule one, never open the glass doors after one.
items.screen: Gus: "Shut the door. Rule 1, never open the glass doors after 1." (rule-1 pinned bar highlighted)

items.text: How did he know? He wasn't even in the building.
items.screen: Lena CU, suspicious, looking up at the ceiling

items.text: I kicked the door shut, but the elevator kept coming, and it opened on the lobby with nobody inside.
items.screen: Door bolt flash; elevator doors slide open on an empty lit car

items.text: Gus: Rule two. If the elevator comes down empty, don't get in.
items.screen: Rule-2 bubble pops: "2. If the elevator comes down empty, don't get in."

items.text: So I stayed in my chair. Inside the car, the button for nineteen was already lit.
items.screen: Car panel insert: button 19 glowing orange, nobody inside

items.text: And the doors stayed open, waiting, until I looked away. Then it climbed straight back to nineteen.
items.screen: Doors hold open (no timer runs out); the moment the camera cuts to Lena looking down, the doors close; display climbs to 19

items.text: One small rule broken, and the building answered in seconds. After that, I read every rule twice.
items.screen: Chat pulls out to show all six rule bubbles; ticks appear beside 1 and 2

items.text: Rule four was about the key board behind me. At three, count the keys: ninety-five, and if there's a ninety-sixth, don't touch it.
items.screen: Key board: 96 numbered hooks, 95 keys, one empty hook; rule-4 bubble "4. At 3, count the keys. 95. If there's a 96th, don't touch it."

items.text: And on the desk phone, the button for nineteen-oh-three had a strip of yellow tape over it. Old tape, curling at one corner.
items.screen: Desk-phone close-up: rows of unit buttons "1901 1902 [tape] 1904"; the tape's curled corner

items.text: At two forty-one, the work phone buzzed. A text from a contact already saved as Mr. Pell, owner.
items.screen: Desk clock 2:41; new thread "Mr. Pell (Owner)" with a saved-contact card

items.text: Nineteen-oh-three needs help. Go up now.
items.screen: Pell: "1903 needs help. Go up now."

items.text: Rule five. If Mr. Pell, the owner, texts you, do what he says.
items.screen: Rule-5 bubble highlighted: "5. If Mr. Pell, the owner, texts you, do what he says."

items.text: So rule five said go up, and rule three said nobody goes up. The same man wrote both. One of them had to be wrong.
items.screen: Whip between the rule-5 and rule-3 bubbles, both highlighted

items.text: I asked Gus which rule wins. He started typing. Stopped. Started again.
items.screen: Me: "The owner says go up. Which rule wins?"; header "Gus is typing…" on, off, on
Typing dots, no VO

items.text: Gus: What number texted you?
items.screen: Gus: "What number texted you?"

items.text: I sent him a screenshot.
items.screen: My screenshot bubble: the Pell contact card, number visible (it will not match the staff sheet in Part 2)

items.text: That number was never his.
items.screen: Gus: "That number was never his." (glitch, shake)

items.text: So neither rule was wrong. The number was.
items.screen: Lena CU, shocked

items.text: Gus: Don't go up. Don't send anyone.
items.screen: Gus: "Don't go up. Don't send anyone."

items.text: I typed, and if nineteen-oh-three calls? And he didn't answer.
items.screen: Me: "and if 1903 calls?" (delivered, no reply)

items.text: I checked the camera monitor. On nineteen, the door to nineteen-oh-three was open a crack, and a man in a concierge blazer stood beside it, facing the wall.
items.screen: Monitor: 2x3 CCTV grid, zoom into "CAM 19-E"; grey hallway, 1903's door ajar, a back-view man in a navy blazer facing the wall beside it
HELD 3.8 s, music out: the dark gap of 1903's door widens slowly while the man does not move

items.text: Then Pell again. Gus doesn't work here anymore. Ask him why he left at two forty-one last night.
items.screen: Pell: "Gus doesn't work here anymore. Ask him why he left at 2:41 last night."

items.text: Two forty-one, the exact same minute, twenty-four hours ago.
items.screen: Desk clock 2:41 in red, then "-24 h"

items.text: I called building security and got a recording. Next patrol, six a.m.
items.screen: Call screen "Calloway Security · recording"; "Next patrol 6:00 AM"

items.text: I typed to Gus, why did you leave? And his little green dot went grey.
items.screen: Me: "why did you leave?"; Gus's header goes from "online" to "last seen 2:38"

items.text: Then the desk phone made a sound I'd never heard it make. Under the yellow tape, a light was glowing red.
items.screen: Lobby wide, lights dip; then the desk-phone ECU, red light through the tape
Ring; LCD "LINE 1903"; no VO

items.text: It was line nineteen-oh-three, and Gus's dot flicked back to green.
items.screen: Gus's header: "online"; typing dots

items.text: Let it ring.
items.screen: Gus: "Let it ring." Push past it to the rule-3 bubble over the red-lit button (frame-0 framing); card "PART 1/2"
Hold the bookend; hard cut to black

beats.title: B1 COLD HOOK: the rule, the call, a defied order, the voice
B5 RIVAL AUTHORITIES (read-out rhythm)
B4 OUTSIDE CHECK on paper (HEARSE-P2 1:36-1:47)
B5 COUNT LADDER + PART-1 PLANTS PAID
B7 LULL + PAPER PLANT (the log)
B8 MIDPOINT REFRAME: rule 3 inverted
B5 RULE-BREAK LADDER (each rule named as it breaks)
B9 PEAK: the man in the blazer (held 4 s)
B10 LIFELINE (removed)
B11 TWIST: the voice was the lure, the chat was protecting her
B12 CLIFF + BOOKEND: a new rule from a new authority

items.text: Our front desk phone was ringing from nineteen-oh-three. My handover rules swore nineteen-oh-three was empty.
items.screen: FRAME 0 = COVER: desk-phone ECU, red light through the yellow tape, LCD "LINE 1903 · CALLING"; behind it the work phone with the rule-3 bubble

items.text: Gus said let it ring, and I picked up.
items.screen: Gus's bubble "Let it ring." on the propped phone; Lena lifts the receiver

items.text: Kid, it's Gus. Whatever's in that chat, it isn't me.
items.screen: Lena CU, receiver to her ear; LCD "1903 · 00:04" (line hiss)

items.text: Then a click, and the line went dead.
items.screen: LCD "LINE DROPPED"; the red light snaps off

items.text: Then the handover chat buzzed. Gus: That wasn't me on the phone. I'm home in bed. Don't pick up again.
items.screen: Gus: "That wasn't me on the phone. I'm home in bed. Don't pick up again."

items.text: Then the owner, Pell: Gus never came home last night. Go up.
items.screen: Thread "Mr. Pell (Owner)": "Gus never came home last night. Go up."

items.text: Two Guses and one owner. So which Gus was in my chat? Somebody was lying to me.
items.screen: Lena CU, eyes left / right

items.text: Under the desk there's a laminated staff sheet. It's paper, and nobody can edit paper.
items.screen: Tilt down under the desk: a laminated sheet "CALLOWAY STAFF · EMERGENCY CONTACTS" in phone-torch light

items.text: Mr. Pell's real number was on it. It wasn't the number that had been texting me.
items.screen: Sheet row "R. Pell (Owner)" with a number; side by side with the Pell contact card: the numbers differ (red strike on the contact)

items.text: Gus's cell was on it too, so I dialed it.
items.screen: Row "G. Brandt (Night) · cell" highlighted; call screen "Gus Brandt · calling…"

items.text: It rang, and at the exact same second, under the yellow tape, line nineteen-oh-three lit up.
items.screen: Split screen: work phone "calling…" / desk-phone 1903 light, pulsing together

items.text: His phone was up there, so the Gus in my chat lied too. He wasn't home in bed.
items.screen: Gus's bubble "I'm home in bed." edited to red: "I'm home in bed. ✕"

items.text: At three a.m., rule four: count the keys. Ninety-five, and if there's a ninety-sixth, don't touch it.
items.screen: Desk clock 3:00; rule-4 bubble "4. At 3, count the keys. 95. If there's a 96th, don't touch it."; key board

items.text: Ninety-three. Ninety-four. Ninety-five.
items.screen: Count overlay 93 · 94 · 95, one hook lighting per count
Near-black beat, one brass glint

items.text: Ninety-six.
items.screen: "96" in red; the extra key swings on hook 96

items.text: The extra key had a brass tag that said nineteen-oh-three.
items.screen: Brass tag "1903" ECU

items.text: Behind me, the elevator chimed. It had come down from nineteen, empty, and it held its doors open for me.
items.screen: Lena turns; the elevator doors open on an empty lit car; button 19 lit inside

items.text: The key, the elevator, the owner. Everything in this building was pointing up.
items.screen: Triptych: brass tag / open car / Pell bubble, each pops on its word; arrows up

items.text: I opened the visitor log so my hands had something to do. Gus's last entry was from last night.
items.screen: Visitor log, pages turning back to yesterday

items.text: Two forty-one, nineteen-oh-three called, going up myself, back in five.
items.screen: Handwriting writes on: "2:41 – 1903 called. Going up myself. Back in five. –G"

items.text: He never signed back in.
items.screen: The empty TIME IN cell

items.text: That's when I got it. Rule three says send nobody up, so Gus didn't send anybody. He went himself.
items.screen: Lena CU, shocked to angry; rule-3 bubble over her

items.text: And rule three is why nobody ever went up after him.
items.screen: Rule-3 bubble: "send nobody up" glows red

items.text: Pell lied about everything else, but he was right about one thing. Somebody had to go up.
items.screen: Pell's "Go up now." bubble; Lena stands

items.text: I took the ninety-sixth key, rule four. I got into the empty elevator, rule two.
items.screen: Hook 96 empties; stamp "4 ✕ the 96th key"; elevator doors; stamp "2 ✕ rode it empty"

items.text: I left the desk before seven, rule six. And I sent somebody up. Me. Rule three.
items.screen: Empty desk, chair turning; stamp "6 ✕ left the desk"; then the big red stamp "3 ✕ sent somebody up: me"

items.text: The chat lit up. Gus: Put the key back, please. Nobody means you too.
items.screen: Gus: "Put the key back, please. Nobody means you too."

items.text: Five, nine, and at thirteen the lights dipped. At sixteen my signal died, but the chat kept working. How?
items.screen: Floor display 5 > 9 > 13 (light dip) > 16 (status bar "No Service"); the chat still delivers

items.text: Gus: If I'm standing up there, it isn't me.
items.screen: Gus: "If I'm standing up there, it isn't me."

items.text: At nineteen, the doors opened on a hallway with one light on.
items.screen: Display 19; doors part on the hallway

items.text: At the far end, outside nineteen-oh-three, a man in a concierge blazer stood with his face to the wall.
items.screen: Hallway, one light; door plate 1903 ajar; the back-view blazer man beside it, facing the wall
HELD 4.0 s, music out, heartbeat only; slow push 1.00 > 1.04

items.text: Four percent battery and no signal. I dialed nine-one-one anyway, and the call failed.
items.screen: Battery 4% red; call "911 · Call failed"

items.text: He didn't turn around. He just said, softly, in Gus's voice:
items.screen: Hallway, very slow push; no lip flap

items.text: Thanks, kid. Your shift now.
items.screen: Caption only; the man stays facing the wall

items.text: Then the hallway light went out.
items.screen: Black; phone glow from below on Lena

items.text: The chat buzzed one last time. Gus: I'm sorry. I lied so you wouldn't come.
items.screen: Gus: "I'm sorry. I lied so you wouldn't come."

items.text: Then the handover chat added a new member, Marcus from the day shift. And a message started sending, from me.
items.screen: Banner "Marcus (Day Desk) joined Desk Handover"; header "3 members"; my outgoing bubble with a sending spinner

items.text: The same six rules, word for word, except rule three. If nineteen-oh-three calls, send nobody up. Even if it sounds like me.
items.screen: Rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 stack in exactly as in Part 1, sent by Lena; last bubble: "3. If 1903 calls, send nobody up. Even if it sounds like me."; card "END · PART 2/2"
Faint ring of line 1903 under the bookend; hard cut
